If you choose credit card, enter your credit card information.

result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.

result.rule: When the description states that two or more actions occur at the same time, or that one action is independent of another after a shared prerequisite: Model the actions on separate branches from a parallel gateway. Use a parallel join only before a continuation that requires all those branches to finish.

When the description names multiple required activities that must be completed before a later activity, without specifying an order among them: Model the activities as separate parallel branches and synchronize them before the later activity.

When the description states that a participant enters information or other inputs as a distinct action: Model that action as a separate activity in the appropriate sequence; do not omit it or absorb it into another activity.

When the description presents mutually exclusive alternatives for where or how an item is handled: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway and separate alternative paths, then merge them before any shared next step.
